arxiv-2112-02225.description: Abstract Deep hashing has shown promising performance in large-scale image retrieval. However, latent codes extracted by D eep N eural N etworks (DNNs) will inevitably lose semantic information during the binarization process, which damages the retrieval accuracy and makes it challenging.

arxiv-2405-05005.title: Analyzing Design Principles for Competitive Evolution Strategies in Constrained Search Spaces
arxiv-2405-05005.creator: Michael Hellwig, Hans-Georg Beyer
arxiv-2405-05005.description: Abstract . In the context of the 2018 IEEE Congress of Evolutionary Computation, the Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy for constrained optimization turned out to be notably successful in the competition on constrained single objective real-parameter optimization. Across all considered instances the so-called ϵ \epsilon MAg-ES achieved the second rank.

arxiv-2405-11578.title: Random Attention Span Thanks: I would like to thank Victor Aguiar, Maria Goltsman, Nail Kashaev, Roy Allen, Elliot Lipnowski and John Quah for useful comments and suggestions. I am grateful to Victor Aguiar, Nail Kashaev, Maria Jose Boccardi and Jeongbin Kim for providing their experimental dataset
arxiv-2405-11578.creator: Dazhuo Wei
arxiv-2405-11578.description: Abstract In this paper, I introduce a random attention span model (RAS) which uses stopping time to identify decision-makers’ behavior under limited attention. Unlike many limited attention models, the RAS identifies preferences using time variation without any need for menu variation. In addition, the RAS allows the consideration set to be correlated with the preference.

arxiv-2406-19973.title: Self-Training Large Language and Vision Assistant for Medical Question-Answering
arxiv-2406-19973.creator: Guohao Sun, Can Qin, Huazhu Fu, Linwei Wang, Zhiqiang Tao
arxiv-2406-19973.description: Abstract Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have shown significant potential in assisting medical diagnosis by leveraging extensive biomedical datasets. However, the advancement of medical image understanding and reasoning critically depends on building high-quality visual instruction data, which is costly and labor-intensive to obtain, particularly in the medical domain.

arxiv-2408-10518.title: BAUST Lipi: A BdSL Dataset with Deep Learning Based Bangla Sign Language Recognition
arxiv-2408-10518.creator: 1 st Md Hadiuzzaman, 2 nd Mohammed Sowket Ali, 4 nd Tamanna Sultana, 6 nd Abdur Raj Shafi, 3 rd Abu Saleh Musa Miah, 5 th Jungpil Shin
arxiv-2408-10518.description: Abstract People commonly communicate in English, Arabic, and Bengali spoken languages through various mediums. However, deaf and hard-of-hearing individuals primarily use body language and sign language to express their needs and achieve independence. Sign language research is burgeoning to enhance communication with the deaf community.

arxiv-2505-02492.title: Uncertainty in Repeated Implicit Feedback as a Measure of Reliability
arxiv-2505-02492.creator: Bruno Sguerra, Viet-Anh Tran, Romain Hennequin, Manuel Moussallam
arxiv-2505-02492.description: Abstract . Recommender systems rely heavily on user feedback to learn effective user and item representations. Despite their widespread adoption, limited attention has been given to the uncertainty inherent in the feedback used to train these systems. Both implicit and explicit feedback are prone to noise due to the variability in human interactions, with implicit feedback being particularly challenging.

arxiv-2506-14988.title: Fair Algorithms with Probing for Multi-Agent Multi-Armed Bandits
arxiv-2506-14988.creator: Tianyi Xu, Jiaxin Liu, Zizhan Zheng
arxiv-2506-14988.description: Abstract We propose a multi-agent multi-armed bandit (MA-MAB) framework aimed at ensuring fair outcomes across agents while maximizing overall system performance. A key challenge in this setting is decision-making under limited information about arm rewards. To address this, we introduce a novel probing framework that strategically gathers information about selected arms before allocation.

arxiv-2510-03826.title: Fourier-Galerkin method for scattering poles of sound soft obstacles Thanks: The research of Y. Ma was supported by the NSFC under grant No.11901085. The research of J. Sun was partially supported by an NSF Grant DMS-2109949 and a SIMONS Foundation Collaboration Grant 711922.
arxiv-2510-03826.creator: Yunyun Ma, Jiguang Sun
arxiv-2510-03826.description: Abstract The computation of scattering poles for a sound-soft obstacle is investigated. These poles correspond to the eigenvalues of two boundary integral operators. We construct novel decompositions of these operators and show that they are Fredholm. Then a Fourier-Galerkin method is proposed for discretization.

arxiv-2510-04980.title: LLM-Hanabi : Evaluating Multi-Agent Gameplays with Theory-of-Mind and Rationale Inference in Imperfect Information Collaboration Game
arxiv-2510-04980.creator: Fangzhou Liang, Tianshi Zheng, Chunkit Chan, Yauwai Yim, Yangqiu Song
arxiv-2510-04980.description: Abstract Effective multi-agent collaboration requires agents to infer the rationale behind others’ actions, a capability rooted in Theory-of-Mind (ToM). While recent Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at logical inference, their ability to infer rationale in dynamic, collaborative settings remains under-explored. This study introduces LLM-Hanabi 1 1 1 https://github.

pmc-12458808.title: LTO1 and YAE1 regulate MHC-I expression via nonsense-mediated RNA decay in tumor cells
pmc-12458808.creator: Zhengning Yang, Zhongxuan Meng, Shangyuan Liu, Yuxin Chen, Xuhong Gan, Zi‑Mei Zhang, Xiaoshan Luo, Jiahong Yan, Huijin Chen, Danqing Huang, Lihong Huang, Xiaomin Zeng, Wenyu Ma, Jun Liu, Linlin Wang, Haotian Huang, Xinyi Yang, Mei Hu, Lin Chen, Hongli Du, Qibin Leng, Li Qiu, Xiaoling Wang
pmc-12458808.description: BackgroundNonsense-mediated messenger RNA decay (NMD) is a highly conserved surveillance system that degrades mRNAs with premature termination codons (PTCs), and regulates the mRNA quantity. Cancer cells hijack NMD to compensate for the imbalanced DNA levels and modulate their antigenicity. We identified the LTO1/YAE1 complex as NMD factors regulating ribosome biogenesis.

pmc-12568673.title: Case Report: E2 luteal phase priming in a stop GnRH agonist combined with GnRH antagonist using a delta follitropin protocol in a poor responder: clinical case
pmc-12568673.creator: Melissa María Morales Berrocal, Mariana Peña Miranda, Armando Miguel Roque Sánchez
pmc-12568673.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). A 30-year-old woman with a body mass index of 20.6 kg/m² consulted due to two years of primary infertility. The patient had a history of two unsuccessful previous rounds of ovarian stimulation for IVF due to poor ovarian response. A novel ovarian stimulation approach incorporating luteal phase estradiol priming in a stop GnRH agonist plus delta follitropin-GnRH antagonist protocol was followed. in vitro fertilization was performed resulting in eight mature oocytes, which were fertilized and developed into two usable blasts.

pmc-12596618.title: Using Implementation Science to Understand Barriers to Telemedicine Use for Burn Care During a Crisis
pmc-12596618.creator: Amanda P Bettencourt, Theresa M Davis, Subhash Aryal, Joseph Rhodes, Mark J Johnston, Cindy Wegryn, Matthew D Supple, Victor C Joe, John Schulz, Gary Vercruysse, Deena Kelly Costa, Colleen Ryan
pmc-12596618.description: During a crisis, hospitals need help to meet the needs of patients with burns. Very few clinicians (1%) of medical doctors and registered nurses and few hospitals (2%) have burn care expertise. Due to these capacity limitations, patients with burns as extensive as 40% TBSA remain outside of burn centers for days to weeks before reaching definitive care.

pmc-12703940.title: From dispenser to nest: collection of fumigated material repels parasites across behavioural traits in Darwin’s finches
pmc-12703940.creator: Lauren K Common, Sonia Kleindorfer, Andrew C Katsis, Katherine Albán Morales, Dominique M E Quirola, Birgit Fessl
pmc-12703940.description: In the midst of a biodiversity crisis, it is important to conserve diversity at all levels, including species, genetic, and behavioural diversity. Animals with different behavioural traits can interact with their environment in distinct ways; hence, the distribution of behavioural traits within a population can influence the efficacy and outcome of conservation interventions.

pmc-13391209.title: Long-term efficacy and safety of left atrial appendage closure vs. oral anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-13391209.creator: Paschalis Karakasis, Stylianos Tzeis, Athanasios Samaras, Konstantinos Vlachos, Konstantinos Pamporis, Panagiotis Theofilis, Apostolos Tzikas, Antonios P Antoniadis, Pierre Jaïs, Nikolaos Fragakis
pmc-13391209.description: AimsLeft atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as an alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC) for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF), but its long-term comparative efficacy remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing LAAC with OAC in AF.

pmc-13581938.title: Fulminant group A streptococcal necrotizing fasciitis presenting as severe calf pain after pharyngitis in an adolescent: a case report
pmc-13581938.creator: Lisa Roncoroni, Jan Kühle, Lampros Kousoulas, Katharina Müller-Peltzer, Dawid L. Staudacher
pmc-13581938.description: BackgroundInvasive Group A Streptococcus (GAS) infection can rapidly progress to life-threatening conditions, including necrotizing fasciitis (NF) and streptococcal toxic shock syndrome (STSS). While typically associated with cutaneous breaches or underlying comorbidities, hematogenous seeding following primary pharyngeal infection is a rare but documented phenomenon. Early diagnosis is often complicated by subtle skin changes and the rarity of the disease.
